summary: Elevated 5xx and streaming disconnects on mixed chat+embedding route after priority-shed weight miscalculation
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (primarily OrionHealth enterprise tenant) began reporting increased 5xx responses and streaming session disconnects on the mixed chat+embedding route between 2026-03-13T16:05 and 2026-03-13T18:30 UTC. Errors spiked from baseline ~0.2% to ~8% for the route; several long-lived streaming sessions observed abrupt RSTs followed by short lived runtime restarts.

Impact:
- OrionHealth: intermittent failures while generating clinical summarizations (chat) and uploading embedding batches; user-facing errors and timeouts.
- Platform: elevated 5xx floor on the route in us-east for ~2.5 hours; increased latency and partial degradation of streaming.

Environment:
- prod:us-east (primary)
- Route: /v1/chat+embed (mixed route; hedged retries enabled)
- Models in use: open-vicuna-13b for chat, redwood-embedding-v2 for embeddings

Steps to reproduce (observed by SRE):
1) Replayed a tenant-weighted steady-state traffic mix (60% short-chat, 30% embeddings, 10% long-chat streaming) against staging priority scheduler with the same weights that were rolled to prod.
2) Increased small long-lived streaming connections to simulate real customer sessions.
3) Observed accept-queue pressure at the API gateway and concurrent hedged retries from the edge when priority weights dipped below threshold.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returned 502/503/504 for new requests; streaming connections experienced half-open socket resets.
- Serving runtime processes logged SIGTERM sequences and then restarted on some GPU workers (graceful exit did not complete before watchdog timed out).
- Priority scheduler metrics showed negative "available slots" in the shim for a short period due to a weight normalization bug (see investigation).

Logs and artifacts:
- Sample gateway trace: trace_id=trace-20260313-6731 (attached)
- Runtime logs: gpu_worker_77: "watchdog: restart requested after accept loop stall" (attached snippet)
- Dashboard: /dashboards/ingress/priority-shed-2026-03-13 (attached)
investigation_notes:
Timeline and quick findings:
- 16:05 UTC: first elevated error alerts from routing monitors.
- 16:07 UTC: hedged-retry counter for route rose x12 over baseline, backlog in accept queue increased.
- 16:12 UTC: SRE replayed the weight calculation for the priority scheduler and found an edge case where floating-point rounding produced a transient negative "available_slot" after normalizing tenant weights when combined with dynamic burst credits. This caused the priority-shed shim to mark some low-latency routes as ineligible which triggered large-batch hedged retries from the edge.
- 16:20-17:30 UTC: multiple serving runtime processes received surge of concurrent connections; some obeyed graceful shutdown but several hit the runtime watchdog and restarted, amplifying rate of 5xx.
- Hypothesis: priority-scheduler miscalculation -> misclassification of route eligibility -> hedged retries + accept-queue overload -> runtime watchdog-triggered restarts -> elevated 5xx floor.
- Corroborating evidence: matched timestamps across scheduler logs (scheduler-2) and gateway (apigw-10); PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/priority-scheduler/pull/498 contains the normalization change deployed in the previous sweep.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- At 16:30 UTC: applied an emergency soft-cap on hedged-retry amplification in the edge (reduced hedged retry fanout for affected route) — reduced immediate pressure on accept queues.
- At 16:45 UTC: increased accept-queue depth on the API gateway for prod:us-east for the mixed route and tuned watchdog timeout on two suspect GPU worker pools. Both reduced restarts but did not fully clear the error floor.

Next steps planned:
1) Roll back the weight-normalization microchange from PR 498 in a controlled canary (SRE scheduled at 2026-03-14T02:00 UTC).
2) Add defensive clamp to priority scheduler to ensure available_slot >= 0 and log telemetry on negative occurrences.
3) Add unit tests for mixed-weight + burst-credit paths.
4) Postmortem draft and customer communication for OrionHealth.
resolution: Work-in-progress: temporary edge hedged-retry cap and accept-queue tuning reduced immediate customer impact. A rollback of the priority-scheduler normalization change is scheduled for 2026-03-14 UTC; permanent fixes include clamping, tests, and a telemetry alert for negative available_slot events. Documented followups for postmortem and retro.

2026-03-13 16:35 UTC - SRE (Luca Moreno): Initial triage shows accept-queue growth and hedged-retry amplification for /v1/chat+embed. Suspect priority scheduler weight normalization. Pulling scheduler logs now.

2026-03-13 16:50 UTC - OrionHealth (customer): We've observed failed clinical summary exports at ~16:10-16:40 UTC. Any ETA on mitigation? This impacts our reporting pipeline.
Support provided temporary suggestion: switch to chat-only route as workaround (not ideal).
2026-03-13 17:05 UTC - Support (Maya Patel): Applied hedged-retry cap at edge; monitoring for error-rate drop. Customer informed; asked to validate if retries stop on their side.

2026-03-13 17:20 UTC - SRE (Luca Moreno): Hedged cap reduced 5xx from ~8% to ~1.5% over 10 minutes. Watching for runtime restarts. Opening rollback window for scheduler microchange. Linking PR 498 in investigation.

2026-03-14 02:05 UTC - SRE (Luca Moreno): Rolled back normalization change to canary subset; no negative available_slot events in canary for 30m and canary error-rate stable. Preparing full rollback and postmortem notes.

2026-03-14 08:30 UTC - Support (Maya Patel): Customer notified of temporary mitigation and rollback schedule; provided workaround guidance and committed to postmortem. Customer acknowledged and requested timeline for permanent fix.
